arxiv-1501-06766.title: Graded Version of Some Basic Theorems on Local Cohomology to a Pair of Ideals
arxiv-1501-06766.creator: P. H. Lima and V. H. Jorge Pérez
arxiv-1501-06766.description: Abstract In this paper, we prove some well-known results on local cohomology with respect to a pair of ideals in graded version, such as, Independence Theorem, Lichtenbaum-Harshorne Vanishing Theorem, Basic Finiteness and Vanishing Theorem, among others. Besides, we present a generalized version of Melkersson Theorem about Artinianess of modules and a result concerning Artinianess of local cohomology modules.

arxiv-2011-03304.title: Mixed Convection in a Differentially Heated Cavity with Local Flow Modulation via Rotating Flat Plates
arxiv-2011-03304.creator: Md. Azizul Hakim, Atiqul Islam Ahad, Abrar Ul Karim, Mohammad Nasim Hasan
arxiv-2011-03304.description: Abstract Mixed Convection inside a cavity resulting from thermal buoyancy force under local modulation via rotating flat plate has been investigated. The present model consists of a square cavity with the left and right vertical walls fixed at constant high and low temperatures respectively while the top and bottom walls are supposed to be adiabatic.

arxiv-2105-07504.title: Mean curvature flow in Homology and foliations of hyperbolic 3 3 -manifolds Thanks: FVP was supported by the Minerva Research Foundation and by NSF grant DMS-2001997.
arxiv-2105-07504.creator: Marco A. M. Guaraco, Vanderson Lima, Franco Vargas Pallete
arxiv-2105-07504.description: Abstract . We study global aspects of the mean curvature flow of non-separating hypersurfaces S S in closed manifolds. For instance, if S S has non-vanishing mean curvature, we show its level set flow converges smoothly towards an embedded minimal hypersurface Γ \Gamma . We prove a similar result for the flow with surgery in dimension 2.

arxiv-2203-03978.title: Contrastive Conditional Neural Processes
arxiv-2203-03978.creator: Zesheng Ye, Lina Yao
arxiv-2203-03978.description: Abstract Conditional Neural Processes (CNPs) bridge neural networks with probabilistic inference to approximate functions of Stochastic Processes under meta-learning settings. Given a batch of non- i.i.d function instantiations, CNPs are jointly optimized for in-instantiation observation prediction and cross-instantiation meta-representation adaptation within a generative reconstruction pipeline.

arxiv-2207-06713.title: Collimation of the kiloparsec-scale radio jets in NGC 2663 2022 Collimation of the kiloparsec-scale radio jets in NGC 2663 – References
arxiv-2207-06713.creator: Velibor Velović, M. D. Filipović, L. Barnes, R. P. Norris, C. D. Tremblay, G. Heald, L. Rudnick, S. S. Shabala, T. G. Pannuti, H. Andernach, O. Titov, S. G. H. Waddell, B. S. Koribalski, D. Grupe, T. Jarrett, R. Z. E. Alsaberi, E. Carretti, J. D. Collier, S. Einecke, T. J. Galvin, A. Hotan, P. Manoj
arxiv-2207-06713.description: Abstract We present the discovery of highly-collimated radio jets spanning a total of 355 kpc around the nearby elliptical galaxy NGC 2663, and the possible first detection of recollimation on kiloparsec scales. The small distance to the galaxy ( ∼ \sim 28.5 Mpc) allows us to resolve portions of the jets to examine their structure.

arxiv-2305-01900.title: Demonstrating repetitive non-destructive readout (RNDR) with SiSeRO devices
arxiv-2305-01900.creator: Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Sven Herrmann, Peter Orel, Kevan Donlon, Gregory Prigozhin, R. Glenn Morris, Michael Cooper, Beverly LaMarr, Andrew Malonis, Steven W. Allen, Marshall W. Bautz, Chris Leitz
arxiv-2305-01900.description: Abstract We demonstrate so-called repetitive non-destructive readout (RNDR) for the first time on a Single electron Sensitive Readout (SiSeRO) device. SiSeRO is a novel on-chip charge detector output stage for charge-coupled device (CCD) image sensors, developed at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. This technology uses a p-MOSFET transistor with a depleted internal gate beneath the transistor channel.

arxiv-2305-09302.title: Pink-Eggs Dataset V1: A Step Toward Invasive Species Management Using Deep Learning Embedded Solutions
arxiv-2305-09302.creator: Di Xu *, Yang Zhao, Xiang Hao, Xin Meng
arxiv-2305-09302.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Di Xu *, Yang Zhao, Xiang Hao, Xin Meng. We introduce a novel dataset consisting of images depicting pink eggs that have been identified as Pomacea canaliculata eggs, accompanied by corresponding bounding box annotations. The purpose of this dataset is to aid researchers in the analysis of the spread of Pomacea canaliculata species by utilizing deep learning techniques, as well as supporting other investigative pursuits that require visual data pertaining to the eggs of Pomacea canaliculata.

arxiv-2404-07157.title: Local probe of bulk and edge states in a fractional Chern insulator
arxiv-2404-07157.creator: Zhurun Ji, Heonjoon Park, Mark E. Barber, Chaowei Hu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jiun-Haw Chu, Xiaodong Xu, Zhi-xun Shen
arxiv-2404-07157.description: Abstract Fractional quantum Hall effect (FQHE) is a prime example of topological quantum many-body phenomena, arising from the interplay between strong electron correlation, topological order, and time reversal symmetry breaking. Recently, a lattice analog of FQHE at zero magnetic field has been observed, confirming the existence of a zero-field fractional Chern insulator (FCI).

inge-christian-mysticism-1899.creator: W.R. Inge
inge-christian-mysticism-1899.description: Inge's 1899 Bampton Lectures on Christian mysticism — the Dean of St. Paul's landmark history from the Fathers to the moderns.

pmc-11354351.title: Transglutaminase 2 Regulates HSF1 Gene Expression in the Acute Phase of Fish Optic Nerve Regeneration
pmc-11354351.creator: Kayo Sugitani, Takumi Mokuya, Yu Kanai, Yurina Takaya, Yuya Omori, Yoshiki Koriyama
pmc-11354351.description: Fish retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) can regenerate after optic nerve lesions (ONLs). We previously reported that heat shock factor 1 (HSF1) and Yamanaka factors increased in the zebrafish retina 0.5–24 h after ONLs, and they led to cell survival and the transformation of neuro-stem cells.

pmc-11607077.title: Maternal polycystic ovary syndrome and Offspring’s Risk of Cardiovascular diseases in Childhood and Young Adulthood
pmc-11607077.creator: Fen Yang, Ziliang Wang, Henrik Toft Sørensen, Imre Janszky, Mika Gissler, Wei Yuan, Maohua Miao, Nathalie Roos, Anna-Karin Wikström, Jiong Li, Krisztina D. László
pmc-11607077.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Children born to mothers with polycystic ovary syndrome have a higher prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors and of subclinical cardiovascular disease, but the association between maternal polycystic ovary syndrome and cardiovascular disease in offspring is unclear. We conduct a register-based cohort study of 6 839 703 live singleton births from Denmark (1973–2016) and Sweden (1973–2014) and follow them for up to 48 years.

pmc-12714684.title: Photonic variational quantum eigensolver for NISQ-compatible quantum technology
pmc-12714684.creator: Kang-Min Hu, Min Namkung, Hyang-Tag Lim
pmc-12714684.description: AbstractQuantum computers have the potential to deliver speed-ups for solving certain important problems that are intractable for classical counterparts, making them a promising avenue for advancing modern computation. However, many quantum algorithms require deep quantum circuits, which are challenging to implement on current noisy devices.

pmc-13019412.title: A Pyrimidine-Based Tubulin Inhibitor Shows Potent Anti-Glioblastoma Activity In Vitro and In Vivo
pmc-13019412.creator: Satyanarayana Pochampally, Lawrence M. Pfeffer, Gustavo A. Miranda-Carboni, Macey Daniel, Jazz I. James, Allana Smith, Chuan He Yang, Hannah R. Kelso, Deanna N. Parke, Dong-Jin Hwang, Wei Li, Duane D. Miller
pmc-13019412.description: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive and treatment-resistant brain tumor with few effective therapies. Tubulin polymers are crucial for maintaining cell–cell signaling, cell proliferation, and cell division. Therefore, tubulin has been targeted by medicinal chemists to develop novel therapeutics to treat cancer. In this regard, we developed novel small-molecule tubulin inhibitors as potential therapeutics to treat GBM.

pmc-13328718.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies VX-809 as a candidate dual-pathway modulator in fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy
pmc-13328718.creator: Shunsuke Noda, Kota Imai, Taisei Okino, Taisuke Numao, Theofilos Tourtas, Ursula Schlötzer-Schrehardt, Friedrich Kruse, Noriko Koizumi, Naoki Okumura
pmc-13328718.description: Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) is a progressive degenerative disease of the corneal endothelium and remains a leading indication for corneal transplantation worldwide. FECD is characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, disruption of proteostasis with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and progressive endothelial cell loss; however, no pharmacological therapy is currently available.

pmc-13458815.title: Development of the first myasthenia gravis patient registry in Latvia: a single-centre experience
pmc-13458815.creator: Arta Grosmane-Bataraga, Vladimirs Krutovs, Marija Roddate, Violeta Žukova, Gundega Ķauķe, Ieva Glāzere, Linda Gailīte, Nataļja Kurjāne, Viktorija Ķēniņa
pmc-13458815.description: This study describes the development of Latvia’s first myasthenia gravis (MG) patient registry in a single-centre setting. Adults with confirmed MG were recruited between January 2022 and May 2025 at Pauls Stradiņš Clinical University Hospital. Demographic and clinical data were collected, and patients were assessed using the MGFA Clinical Classification, MG Composite (MGC), MG-ADL, MGQOL15, and Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS).

pmc-13575808.title: Anonymization of Portuguese Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models and Quantum-Enhanced Hybrid Architectures: Comparative Evaluation Study
pmc-13575808.creator: Samer Rahmeh, Felipe Meneguitti Dias, Ramon Alfredo Moreno, Marina De Fatima De Sa Rebelo, Daniela Herrmann, Jose Eduardo Krieger, Marco Antonio Gutierrez, Ivan Steenstra
pmc-13575808.description: BackgroundThe widespread adoption of electronic health records (EHRs) has generated large-scale repositories of highly sensitive clinical information, emphasizing the need for robust anonymization strategies to enable secondary use for research while safeguarding patient privacy. Conventional rule-based and machine learning approaches for deidentifying medical text face limitations with the linguistic complexity, variability, and context dependence inherent to clinical documentation.
